episode_title: Why Sacramento’s Next Decade Could Be Its Biggest Yet | Bryan Flaherty
question: Why is Sacramento Business Journal one of only three growing national business news publications, and how did the decision to charge for internet content from day one contribute to this growth?
transcript_excerpt: We made a great bet back in mid-2015, 2014 when the internet was becoming everything for news. A lot of folks continued to charge for their product and make their internet content free, but we said what's the difference—we're charging for internet content from day one. Our colleagues and friends had a hard time putting that toothpaste back in the tube, but we didn't necessarily have to. That was a great bet that we made. We are one of three business news organizations that are growing—us, The Wall Street Journal, and The New York Times—and we're not doing it through acquisition. We are doing it just purely based on subscription growth and marketing growth.

question: How many Business Journal markets does Advanced Publications operate, and what is the difference in coverage between markets with publishers versus digital-only markets?
transcript_excerpt: There are 46 now. We actually just opened Fort Worth Business Journal. Currently we have 40 journals that have publisher and events. When you have a publisher in events, you do have a little bit more—your market share and your impact is much greater. The digital-only markets that we have are sometimes smaller markets. LA, New York, Chicago, we only have a digital market because those newspapers and those legacy journals really dominate there.
